question_text: Was Octopus, the Hong Kong payment card company, hacked?
answer_text: Yes, by its own account. Octopus says it detected a cyberattack on Nov 27 that involved the names and photos of about 7,500 customers and contact details of about 22,000 merchants; it says cards and balances are safe.
label: Confirmed

question_text: Is my Octopus card balance or bank account at risk?
answer_text: Octopus says no credit card or bank account information is affected, it has found no customer financial loss, and card and wallet balances remain protected. For some customers, a bank code and top-up amount may be involved.
label: Confirmed

question_text: How did attackers get into Octopus, and who was behind it?
what_would_settle_it: Octopus, the police or another official source saying how the attackers got in and who they were.

question_text: Was the Octopus customer data copied out or published?
what_would_settle_it: Octopus or an official source saying whether the information was copied out of its systems, or a credible outlet reporting that it has appeared somewhere.

question_text: Which Octopus features are not working?
what_would_settle_it: Octopus naming the features its precautions have affected, and saying when they are back.

question_text: Has Octopus told the police and the privacy commissioner?
answer_text: Octopus says it is keeping the relevant authorities informed. HK01 reports that it has reported the incident to the police and notified the privacy commissioner and the Transport and Logistics Bureau; neither body has said so publicly.
label: Reported

answer_text: Watch for unusual account activity and for calls, messages, emails or links claiming to be from Octopus, and do not give out personal or verification details. Octopus says it will contact affected customers by email or SMS.
label: Confirmed

question_text: Which merchants' details were involved in the Octopus attack?
what_would_settle_it: Octopus or a merchant saying publicly which businesses were affected. Octopus has said only that about 22,000 merchants' contact details are involved.
